rows.title: Mathematics for Computer Science
rows.facts: MIT OCW's Spring2015 6.042J resource links the actual textbook by Eric Lehman, F. Thomson Leighton and Albert R. Meyer. Its title page dates the revision18May2015 and permits access under its stated Creative Commons license. Chapter5 covers induction; section5.4.3 explains the invariant principle by induction on execution length with start-state and preserved-step conditions. Chapter13 covers sums and asymptotics; section13.7 treats asymptotic notation.
rows.qualification: The invariant sentence is the cited text's contextual explanation of a proof method with base and transition obligations. It does not claim an arbitrary predicate is invariant without those obligations. Mathematical induction and state invariance remain mathematical topics in their own inventoried lessons; this reference does not replace their proof mappings.
rows.classification_reason: The complete bibliography row maps a resource's topics to this primer. The contextual invariant explanation is checked directly against the cited section, not used to promote an unproved external theorem.

rows.title: Basic Analysis I
